page: Microsoft Azure E4a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a 102 GB SSD, and virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate moderate performance for single-threaded operations alongside constraints in multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core Geekbench score and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates rank in the average tier. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read performance and poor write performance. Database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving also register in the lower 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4a_v4 offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. The hardware profile is suited for relational databases with moderate transaction volumes, in-memory caching layers with lower write intensity, and general-purpose applications requiring a larger memory footprint without high computational demands.
